rules.title: Pairing
rules.text: Draw exactly two different cards. Card order does not matter. There is exactly one result for each of the 231 unordered pairs among the 22 cards.

rules.title: Wonder spellcasting · ability
rules.text: For a Wonder-granted spell, use the highest of Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma scores when the Wonder is received. If tied, choose one of the tied abilities then; this ability stays selected, and its modifier changes normally when the score changes.

rules.title: Wonder spellcasting · save dc
rules.text: 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your selected ability modifier

rules.title: Wonder spellcasting · attack modifier
rules.text: Your Proficiency Bonus + your selected ability modifier

rules.title: Wonder spellcasting · free casting
rules.text: Unless the outcome says otherwise, cast the specified spell once without expending a spell slot or providing components. Regain the use after finishing a Long Rest. Keep the normal casting time, target limitations, range, duration and Concentration requirements; cast at its normal lowest level unless otherwise stated. The spell does not become a prepared/learned class spell from a free casting alone.

rules.title: Wonder spellcasting · cantrips
rules.text: Permanent learned cantrips follow their normal components and character-level scaling. They use Wonder Spellcasting and do not count against class cantrip limits.

rules.title: Wonder spellcasting · slot based castings
rules.text: When using a permanent Wonder-granted spell slot to cast a spell, normal spell components are required, unless another feature waives them. The spell slot restores after a Long Rest and stays at the fixed level assigned by the Wonder.

rules.title: Wonder spellcasting · rage restriction
rules.text: Normal Rage rules still prohibit casting spells or maintaining Concentration while Raging.

rules.title: Resources · recovery wonders
rules.text: Minor Arcane Recovery and Greater Arcane Recovery allow the character to choose one eligible resource when the Wonder is gained: spell slots, Rage uses, Second Wind uses, or Focus Points. Once per Long Rest, regain one expended unit of the chosen resource using a Bonus Action, not exceeding its maximum. A character with none of those resources receives an innate free spell casting as stated by that outcome.

rules.title: Resources · permanent wonders
rules.text: Expanded Reservoir and Greater Reservoir permanently increase the maximum of exactly one eligible resource chosen when granted: a fixed-level spell slot, Rage use, Second Wind use, or Focus Point. Noncasters may still choose the spell slot and an eligible spell to cast from it.

rules.title: Resources · spell slot
rules.text: Wonder-granted spell slots are separate from regular class spellcasting progression and do not change level. They replenish on a Long Rest, including for Warlocks; they do not become Pact Magic slots.

rules.title: Resources · rage
rules.text: An additional maximum Rage use follows Barbarian Rage recovery (regain one expended use on a Short Rest, all on a Long Rest).

rules.title: Resources · second wind
rules.text: An additional maximum Second Wind use follows Fighter Second Wind recovery (regain one expended use on a Short Rest, all on a Long Rest).

rules.title: Resources · focus point
rules.text: An additional maximum Monk Focus Point follows Monk’s Focus recovery (all expended Focus Points return on a Short or Long Rest).

rules.title: Resources · multiclass
rules.text: A multiclass character can choose a feature they actually possess; they cannot gain an extra Rage, Second Wind, or Focus Point if they lack that class feature.

rules.title: Skill improvement
rules.text: If a Wonder grants skill proficiency or Expertise, proficiency is gained if lacking; if already proficient, gain Expertise. If already Expert, choose another eligible skill. Expertise does not multiply proficiency more than twice. Tool proficiency rewards use their stated separate fallbacks.

rules.title: Feats
rules.text: Five specified Origin Feat rewards are Tough, Savage Attacker, Lucky, Musician, and Alert. If the recipient already possesses the named Origin feat, choose a different eligible 2024 Origin feat not already possessed. The Exceptional General feat reward requires prerequisites and excludes Epic Boon feats.

rules.title: Stacking
rules.text: Different and repeated homebrew Wonder rewards may stack, including maximum HP, class resource maxima, and bonus spell slots. Apply the normal 2024 rules limiting feat repeatability, magic/spell effect overlap, Expertise multiplication and ability-score maximums. There is no custom once-per-Reservoir or no-duplicate reward restriction.

rules.title: Negative effects · general
rules.text: All deck negatives are magical and reversible. They affect the drawing character immediately unless specified otherwise, with no saving throw unless the outcome grants one. A curse cannot permanently erase class levels, subclasses, feats, or learned spells. A suppression ends fully when the curse is cured.

rules.title: Negative effects · minor
rules.text: Generally expires after three completed Long Rests, or earlier with Remove Curse; some events resolve once triggered. Effects such as Exhaustion already suffered are not automatically healed by the curse ending.

rules.title: Negative effects · moderate
rules.text: Expires after seven completed Long Rests or earlier with Remove Curse.

rules.title: Negative effects · major
rules.text: Persists until Greater Restoration, Wish or the outcome’s specific quest-based cure. Remove Curse alone cannot end a Major deck curse.

rules.title: Negative effects · catastrophic
rules.text: Persists until Wish or the outcome’s specific adventure-based cure. Neither Remove Curse nor Greater Restoration alone can end a Catastrophic deck curse.

rules.title: Negative effects · spell exception
rules.text: The above special deck removal rules intentionally override the ordinary 2024 rules for those spells. Wish may remove a deck curse as a permitted special use; normal consequences for Wish still apply.

rules.title: Negative effects · max hp and scores
rules.text: Deck curse reductions to ability scores and maximum HP persist through Long Rests while the curse exists, even though ordinary recovery might otherwise restore them. On removal, those reductions are fully reversed.

rules.title: Negative effects · duration
rules.text: Count completed Long Rests after the effect begins. Once-per-24-hour triggers reset 24 hours after the previous trigger, not with a Long Rest.

rules.title: Negative effects · overlap
rules.text: If multiple active curses impose identical penalties to the same ability, Speed, or maximum HP, use the largest identical penalty unless an outcome expressly instructs stacking; separate curses still require separate removals.

rules.title: Negative effects · quest cures
rules.text: The DM must provide an attainable opportunity for every Major or Catastrophic quest cure. Completing a listed quest ends the whole effect including its associated supernatural changes.

rules.title: Publication note
rules.text: The complete rules text of published spells, Origin feats, Blessings, and Charms remains in the relevant official source. This import includes concise descriptions, names, and book references, not full reprints of copyrighted published feature text.
